results.title: Parallelizing Tool Execution and LLM Generation for Low-Latency Agent Serving (PASTE)
results.summary: Proposes PASTE, a tool-aware agent-serving system that predicts future tool invocations from recurring agent patterns and speculatively executes them in parallel with LLM generation, reporting ~48.5% reduction in task completion time. Authored by SJTU and Microsoft researchers.

results.title: Cost-Aware Speculative Execution for LLM-Agent Workflows: An Integrated Five-Dimension Method
results.summary: Presents a cost-aware speculative execution method for LLM-agent workflows that chain model calls and tool invocations, building on PASTE and B-PASTE by adding cost-awareness to speculation decisions.

results.title: B-PASTE: Beam-Aware Pattern-Guided Speculative Execution for Resource-Constrained LLM Agents
results.summary: Extends PASTE from single-tool speculation to local branch hypotheses (beam search over possible tool calls) under strict resource constraints.

results.title: Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster Agentic Systems
results.summary: Introduces a lossless framework that breaks the strict sequential execution constraint in agentic systems by using faster models to predict and execute likely future actions in parallel, committing only when predictions match.

results.title: W&D: Scaling Parallel Tool Calling for Efficient Deep Research Agents
results.summary: Explores scaling agent width via parallel tool calling for deep research, showing it optimizes end-to-end latency and LLM API cost by reducing sequential calls and token consumption.

results.title: LLMCompiler: An LLM Compiler for Parallel Function Calling
results.summary: The foundational ICML 2024 framework (1.9k stars) that orchestrates parallel function calling with LLMs by automatically identifying which tasks can run concurrently and which are interdependent, achieving latency speedup and cost savings.

results.title: Reducing Latency of LLM Search Agent via Speculation-based Algorithm-System Co-Design (SPAgent)
results.summary: Proposes SPAgent, a two-phase design that jointly reduces LLM inference latency and overlaps external action-execution latency via speculation, cutting inference time by 23.8% and un-overlapped action execution time by 29.4% on average.
